chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): A man frees his slave by manumission upon his death (tadbir), then he needs the price of the slave. He said: 'He sells him.' I said: 'And if he is wealthy regarding the price?' He said: 'If the slave agrees.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a slave who has been manumitted upon death (tadbir) if the master needs money?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the conditions under which a master may sell a slave designated for manumission upon death (tadbir) to recover their value. It establishes that while the master may sell the slave if he needs the funds, the slave’s consent is crucial, particularly if the master is already wealthy and not in dire need. This ruling highlights the balance between the master's financial rights and the slave's dignity in Shia jurisprudence.
